risks.title: High reliance on debt financing
risks.summary: The company heavily relies on debt to fund growth (1.45B$ in acquisitions in 2025), increasing exposure to interest rates and market conditions. Interest expenses have outpaced revenue growth.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is central in the 10-K, with significant increase in interest expenses (+24% YoY to 134.6M USD) and dependence on multiple debt instruments. Recent issuances of 400M (2035 Notes) and 450M (2034 Notes) increase exposure. The Capital category is highly weighted in real estate, especially for acquisition-driven REITs. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Interest rate sensitivity
risks.summary: Borrowing costs rise with interest rates, directly affecting margins and profitability. The company issued notes at 5.6% in 2025, locking in rates ahead of potential macro shifts.
risks.score_rationale: Multiple references to SOFR adjustments, interest rate swaps, and refinancing. The company used hedges (13.6M$ gain on closing swaps in May 2025), but the risk is recurring and intensified by new fixed-rate debt issuance at 5.6% in a macro uncertain environment. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Revenue concentration among a few large tenants
risks.summary: A significant portion of revenue depends on major tenants (mostly investment grade-rated), making the company vulnerable to their strategic decisions, mergers, or financial difficulties, despite strong credit quality.
risks.score_rationale: 66.8% of annualized rent comes from investment grade-rated tenants, indicating high dependency. While this reduces default risk, losing a single large tenant could impact up to 5-10% of annual revenues. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Risk of future financing unavailability
risks.summary: Ability to raise future capital is not guaranteed, which could hinder the acquisition strategy (305 properties/year) or force asset sales. The ATM program (1.75B$) launched in April 2026 signals reliance on capital markets.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly states there is 'no assurance' that financing will be available on favorable terms. This appears in the Liquidity section, a critical point for an externally growing REIT. Credit conditions could tighten rapidly. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Rising impairment provisions
risks.summary: The 4.7M USD increase (65%) in impairments suggests certain assets may be losing future value, affecting rents on specific properties and future disposition gains.
risks.score_rationale: Impairment provision increased by 65% (from 7.2M to 11.9M USD), signaling potential deterioration in certain assets. The 10-K language is cautious, but the signal is concerning and warrants monitoring. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on acquisition-driven growth model
risks.summary: Strategy relies on continuous acquisitions (average cap rate 7.2%); any slowdown in financing access or deal availability could significantly impact the observed 16% YoY growth.
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth largely depends on acquisitions (305 properties, 1.45B$ in 2025, a 12.8% YoY increase). The text acknowledges full impact is delayed, creating risk of misalignment between expenses and revenues. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Currency or liquidity risk on derivative instruments
risks.summary: Use of derivatives to hedge rates and issuances exposes the company to market movements, refinancing risks, and counterparty liquidity risk.
risks.score_rationale: Termination of forward swaps (325M$) to hedge the 2035 Notes, with a 13.6M USD gain in May 2025. This shows active management but also complex exposure to rate and liquidity markets. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Integration and operational risk from rapid acquisitions
risks.summary: Rapid portfolio growth (41 states, 29 sectors) presents integration, operational management, and quality control risks. G&A expenses up 18% reflect these pressures.
risks.score_rationale: 305 acquisitions in one year (41 states, 29 sectors) require complex operational integration. General and administrative expenses increased by 18% (6.9M USD), suggesting growth-related pressures. (default score, to be refined)
